thread:
Maya: Heads-up — I opened a PR to fix the model card examples for Cobalt6b. The issue: the SDK snippet shows the old `generate()` signature and the example outputs are formatted as free-text, but our console now expects structured JSON examples for the parsing guidance. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2345 :eyes:
Liam: Thanks — can you summarize what changes you made so reviewers don't have to read every line?
Maya: Sure — tl;dr:
- Replace `client.generate(prompt)` with `client.responses.create({ input: prompt })` in all SDK snippets (JS + Py).
- Update example outputs to be valid JSON objects with `type`/`content` fields to match the parsing guidance in the runtime docs.
- Add a short note about compatibility: older clients will still work but we recommend migrating.
Raja: Quick question: Cobalt6b has a quantized variant we list as `cobalt6b-quant`. Do we need to call out any output differences for quantized variants (trimming of long tokens, occasional tokenization edge cases)?
Emily: Yes we should. For other cards we added a compatibility note like: "Quantized variants may exhibit ~0.2% higher tokenization variance; validate with your eval prompts." I can paste the wording if folks want it.
Tariq: Also remember SDK v3 changed streaming behaviour — examples that show incremental JSON building need to show how to `buffer` partial chunks and reassemble, otherwise people copy-paste and break. See the streaming best-practices doc: https://internal.redwood.ai/docs/streaming-best-practices
Maya: Good catch. I'll add a short streaming snippet. For JS I'll show `for await (const chunk of stream)` reassembly pattern; for Py a `for chunk in stream:` example.
docs-bot: CI check started for PR #2345 — docs-lint, snippet-tests.
Liam: Can we also add a tiny benchmark line on the card? Something like "median p50 latency for 256-token context on dedicated is ~45ms/token" — we shouldn't put hard SLAs but a ballpark helps customers choose models. Who owns the bench numbers?
Tariq: I can run a quick synthetic with the current runtime image and post numbers by EOD. I'll note the test conditions (batch size 1, fp16, 256 tokens).
Raja: If you're adding the bench note, add a short sentence clarifying region variance and that Dedicated may differ from Hosted.
Emily: For the migration guide section, let's include a diff snippet showing old->new SDK calls. Small code block helps people. Example:
```js
// old
const out = await client.generate(prompt)
// new
const resp = await client.responses.create({ input: prompt })
console.log(resp.output[0].content)
```
Maya: I'll include that. Also fixing a broken internal link in the card that pointed to `docs/model-registry` instead of `docs/model-catalog`. Found it while browsing.
Liam: Awesome. After you push the follow-up commits ping me and I'll do a quick pass. If `docs-lint` flags anything we can iterate.
Maya: Pushed updates: changed snippets, added streaming and quantized note, included the migration diff and a one-line bench placeholder. CI passed snippet-tests but docs-lint flagged an anchor issue — pushed a small anchor rename.
docs-bot: CI for PR #2345 — all checks passed. :white_check_mark:
Raja: Reviewed and left one tiny nit about phrasing in the compatibility note (sent as an in-line suggestion).
Maya: Addressed Raja's nit and updated the compatibility wording to: "Quantized variants can have slightly higher tokenization variance; validate on your prompt set and pin a variant for production."
Liam: LGTM from me. Going to merge once the auto-preview deploy finishes. Thanks everyone! :rocket:
Maya: Thanks all — will follow up with a short blurb for the release notes so product knows the example outputs are now structured JSON (helps integrators).
Tariq: Posted bench numbers in the PR thread and added the exact test command I used.
Emily: Adding a small unit test in the docs repo snippet-tests that asserts example outputs parse as JSON. I'll open a follow-up PR later today.
Maya: Closing the loop — merged and cherry-picked the streaming snippet into the `streaming-guides` page. If you spot anything else ping me in #docs.
